extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of NIH grants (PD/PI, multi‑PD/PIs, Signing Officials, delegates, eRA Commons users) preparing and submitting RPPRs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting NIH Research Performance Progress Reports (Annual, Interim, Final) via eRA Commons, including what information to report, who may initiate/submit, due dates, and special content requirements such as project outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Use to describe a grant’s scientific progress, identify significant changes, report on personnel, and describe plans for the subsequent budget period or year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual RPPR documents accomplishments and compliance for the ongoing budget/project period. Follow the NIH RPPR Instruction Guide; scientific portion instructions are in Chapters 6 and 7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Use as part of the grant closeout process to submit project outcomes in addition to the information submitted on the annual RPPR, except budget and plans for the upcoming year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final RPPR is completed during closeout; it includes project outcomes (see Project Outcomes criterion) and excludes budget and future plans that appear in annual RPPRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when submitting a renewal (Type 2) application. If the Type 2 is not funded, the Interim RPPR will serve as the Final RPPR for the project. If the Type 2 is funded, the Interim RPPR will serve as the annual RPPR for the final year of the previous competitive segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The data elements collected on the Interim RPPR are the same as for the Final RPPR, including project outcomes. The Interim RPPR link appears one day after the project segment end date in the Commons Status tab but before the award has moved to closeout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to submit (submission channel)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no RPPR form available for download. Submit RPPR data through the eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links for each type of RPPR are accessed through the Commons Status tab. The Final RPPR link becomes available in the closeout module once the grant is eligible for closeout. See RPPR User Guide and RPPR Online Help (screenshots and step-by-step instructions) for eRA Commons submission details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may initiate and submit RPPRs; delegation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the project director/principal investigator (PD/PI) or their PD/PI delegate can initiate RPPRs. For multi-PD/PI grants only the Contact PI or the Contact PD/PI’s delegate can initiate the RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signing Officials typically submit the annual RPPR, but may delegate preparation (Delegate Progress Report) to any PD/PI within the organization on behalf of the Contact PD/PI. A PI may delegate the “Progress Report” function to any eRA Commons user in their organization with the Assistant (ASST) role, allowing that ASST to prepare Annual, Interim and Final RPPRs on behalf of the PI. However, only a Signing Official (SO) or PI (if delegated 'Submit by the SO') are allowed to submit the Annual, Interim, and Final RPPRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit (use RPPR User Guide)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the instructions in the RPPR User Guide to submit the RPPR, Interim RPPR or Final RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The User Guide includes instructions for how to submit RPPRs in the eRA Commons, how to complete the web-based forms, and what information is required. Instructions for completing the scientific portion of the report may be found in Chapters 6 and 7. Additional resources: Screen Shots of the R01-like RPPR (PDF), Guide to Categorizing Products in RPPR's Sec. C (PDF), RPPR Online Help, and instructional videos.

rubrics_metrics.name: When (due dates and timelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines vary by award type: SNAP, Non-SNAP, MYF, Interim/Final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamlined Non-Competing Award Process (SNAP) RPPRs are due approximately 45 days before the next budget period start date. Non-SNAP RPPRs are due approximately 60 days before the next budget period start date. Multi-year funded (MYF) RPPRs are due annually on or before the anniversary of the budget/project period start date. Interim and Final RPPRs are due 120 days from the period of performance end date. Exact dates for a specific award are available in grants status in eRA Commons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accomplishments
rubrics_metrics.description: What the RPPR asks about accomplishments: major goals/objectives, what was accomplished, training opportunities, dissemination, and plans for next reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to the RPPR’s specific prompts: What were the major goals and objectives of the project? What was accomplished under these goals? What opportunities for training and professional development did the project provide? How were the results disseminated to communities of interest? What do you plan to do during the next reporting period to accomplish the goals and objectives?

rubrics_metrics.name: Products
rubrics_metrics.description: Report publications, conference papers, presentations, websites, technologies, inventions, patents/licenses, and other products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of products to report include: publications, conference papers, and presentations; website(s) or other Internet site(s); technologies or techniques; inventions, patent applications, and/or licenses; and other products such as data or databases, physical collections, audio or video products, software, models, educational aids or curricula, instruments or equipment, research materials, interventions, or new business creation. See 'Guide to Categorizing Products in RPPR's Sec. C' for classification guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants and Other Collaborating Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Report information on participants and collaborating organizations involved with the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include key personnel and organizations that collaborated on the project per RPPR fields; see RPPR instruction guide and Online Help for required data elements and formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the impact of the project’s work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report demonstrated or anticipated impacts of the research; use clear descriptions suitable for program staff and stakeholders. (See User Guide for the scientific portion framing.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes/Problems (not required for Final or Interim RPPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report substantive changes or problems affecting the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: changes in approach and reasons for change; actual or anticipated problems or delays and actions or plans to resolve them; changes that have a significant impact on expenditures; and significant changes in use or care of human subjects, vertebrate animals, biohazards, and/or select agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgetary Information (not required for Final or Interim RPPR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide budgetary information for the reporting period when required (annual RPPR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget details are part of the Annual RPPR but are not required on Final or Interim RPPRs. See RPPR Instruction Guide for required budget fields and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Outcomes (Final and Interim RPPR requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concise summary of the outcomes or findings of the award, written for the general public in clear and comprehensible language, without including any proprietary, confidential information or trade secrets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project outcome information is required only on Final and Interim RPPRs. This summary will be made public in NIH RePORTER; therefore it must be non-proprietary and suitable for public dissemination. See 'Sample Project Outcomes Summary - RPPR' for examples.
